what: A CHECKLIST ROW WAS NOT MOVED OFF `queued` BY THE PR THAT RESOLVED IT, AND THE REGISTER THEREFORE LIED TOWARD MORE WORK. MEASURED 2026-09-21: row E10 read `queued` while its fix was already merged in #12676 -- the same PR the session handoff described as 'A7's pipeline + close-out contract + E10'. The manager read the ROW, dispatched a lane against it, and the lane correctly reported there was nothing to do. Cost $0.93, which is small; the mechanism is not. [!] THIS IS THE MIRROR OF THE FAILURE THE WHOLE RESET IS ABOUT. The reset's concern is work that silently stops; this is work that silently RESTARTS, and both come from the same root -- the register's state is maintained by hand, by whoever remembers, and nothing ties a row's state to the PR that changed it. A row stuck at `queued` past its fix costs a duplicate dispatch; the same gap in the other direction is a row marked `done` that nobody did. [!] THE CHECKLIST HAS NO `prs` DISCIPLINE EITHER: E10's `prs` array was empty although #12676 carried its fix, so even a reader who doubted the state had nothing to follow. [!] CANDIDATE FIX, not prescribed: a guard that fails when a merged PR's body or commits name a checklist id whose row is still `queued`. That is checkable from git alone and needs no new register.
